glossary.infectious mononucleosis: Glandular fever: an acute EBV infection with sore throat, fever, nodes and fatigue.
glossary.glandular fever: The common name for infectious mononucleosis.
glossary.EBV: Epstein-Barr virus, a gamma-herpesvirus that infects B cells.
glossary.Epstein-Barr virus: A gamma-herpesvirus spread by saliva that causes glandular fever.
glossary.gamma-herpesvirus: A herpesvirus subfamily that infects lymphocytes and stays latent for life.
glossary.kissing disease: Nickname for glandular fever because EBV spreads through saliva.
glossary.posterior cervical lymphadenopathy: Enlarged lymph nodes behind the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
glossary.exudate: White or yellow material on inflamed tonsils.
glossary.palatal petechiae: Tiny red spots of bleeding on the soft palate.
glossary.petechiae: Pinpoint non-blanching red spots from small bleeds.
glossary.maculopapular rash: A rash of flat red patches and small raised bumps.
glossary.amoxicillin: A penicillin antibiotic; causes a rash in EBV infection.
glossary.ampicillin: A penicillin antibiotic closely related to amoxicillin.
glossary.oral hairy leucoplakia: White, corrugated, 'hairy' patch on the side of the tongue linked to EBV.
glossary.splenic rupture: Tearing of the spleen causing internal bleeding; a surgical emergency.
glossary.Kehr's sign: Left shoulder-tip pain from blood irritating the diaphragm, a sign of splenic rupture.
glossary.peritonism: Signs of peritoneal irritation: guarding, rebound and a rigid abdomen.
glossary.quinsy: Peritonsillar abscess, causing trismus, uvula deviation and a muffled voice.
glossary.stridor: High-pitched noisy breathing from upper airway narrowing.
glossary.monospot: Rapid heterophile antibody test for glandular fever.
glossary.monospot test: Rapid heterophile antibody test for glandular fever.
glossary.heterophile antibodies: Non-specific antibodies that agglutinate horse or sheep red cells; detected by the monospot.
glossary.EBV serology: Blood tests for antibodies to EBV antigens such as VCA IgM; gold standard.
glossary.VCA IgM: Antibody to the EBV viral capsid antigen showing recent infection.
glossary.atypical lymphocytes: Large reactive CD8+ T cells seen on the blood film in EBV.
glossary.CD21: Complement receptor 2 on B cells; the entry receptor for EBV.
glossary.CD8+: Marker of cytotoxic T cells that kill virus-infected cells.
glossary.B lymphocytes: Antibody-producing white cells; the cells EBV infects.
glossary.polyclonal: Arising from many different cell clones rather than one.
glossary.lymphoid hyperplasia: Increase in the number of lymphoid cells, enlarging nodes and spleen.
glossary.group and save: Blood group and antibody screen so blood can be issued quickly.
glossary.prednisolone: Oral corticosteroid used for severe tonsillar swelling.
glossary.corticosteroids: Anti-inflammatory steroid drugs such as prednisolone.
glossary.self-limiting: Gets better on its own without specific treatment.
glossary.NICE CKS: NICE Clinical Knowledge Summaries: concise UK primary care guidance.

technique.stem: An 18 year old woman has a 1 week history of sore throat, fever and extreme tiredness. She started university 6 weeks ago. Her tonsils are enlarged with white exudate. There are tender nodes behind both sternocleidomastoid muscles and the spleen tip is palpable.

steps.x: **C. Infectious mononucleosis.** Posterior nodes + spleen + fatigue = EBV.
